TWAP observation configuration, fixed fee-500 pool selection, and resistance to short-term oracle manipulation
Rebalance pricing, strategy-selected ranges, swap execution, and consistency between TWAP outputs and accounted reserves
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: Multipool is the primary component combining user-facing share accounting, Uniswap V3 pricing, reserve calculations, and privileged rebalancing; the annotations explicitly indicate spot-derived reserves and slot0 marks alongside TWAP checks, making it the highest-value unvisited component for price-manipulation analysis. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every path that reads price or reserves and every path that changes pool balances or share value, verify whether attacker-controlled spot state can affect deposits, withdrawals, rebalance decisions, or swap amounts, and document either a concrete exploitable manipulation path with impact or evidence that all relevant paths use manipulation-resistant pricing and enforce consistent accounting.

items.goal: Vulnerability analysis of External users and callers
focus_areas: Caller-controlled deposit and withdrawal flows that derive share value from manipulable token balances or pool prices
Whether users can trigger deposits, withdrawals, or callbacks around spot-price changes to extract disproportionate token value
Interactions between Dispatcher-held LP shares, caller-directed withdrawals, and Uniswap V3 price-sensitive accounting
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: This is an unvisited component and directly exercises the externally reachable value-transfer paths. The graph identifies caller-directed withdrawals, Dispatcher-held LP shares, and withdrawal payments to the caller, while reserve and valuation logic depends on balances and spot-derived prices. These characteristics warrant checking whether an attacker can manipulate prices or balances immediately before a user-directed operation and receive excess assets. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every externally callable user flow through Dispatcher and Multipool state reads, identify all price or reserve inputs and their timing relative to transfers/callbacks, and determine whether any feasible price manipulation changes redemption or deposit value without adequate TWAP, slippage, or share-accounting protection. Record a concrete exploit path or conclude no price-manipulation exposure exists in these flows.

items.goal: Vulnerability analysis of Uniswap V3 underlying pools
focus_areas: Determine whether Multipool pricing, TWAP checks, range initialization, or reserve accounting rely on manipulable pool observations
Trace how short-term liquidity changes, concentrated-liquidity shifts, swaps, and observation cardinality affect the prices consumed by the system
Assess whether an attacker can manipulate the underlying pool price or observations within one transaction or over the TWAP window to influence deposits, withdrawals, rebalances, or swaps
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: The two existing price-manipulation hypotheses depend directly on the underlying Uniswap V3 pool's spot tick and TWAP behavior, while this component has not been selected for a dedicated investigation. EXIT CRITERIA: Establish the exact pool-derived price and observation flows, identify whether supported pools and configured TWAP windows provide manipulation resistance, and either document a concrete exploitable price-manipulation path with affected state transitions or conclude that the pool integration prevents such influence.

focus_areas: Reserve-based deposit and withdrawal share pricing
Snapshot-driven accounting and withdrawal deviation checks
Caller-directed withdrawals and Dispatcher-held LP shares
Manipulation of underlying Multipool reserves or spot-derived values affecting user balances
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: Dispatcher is a critical uncompleted component whose accounting directly prices deposits and withdrawals using reserve-based state, while current hypotheses identify instantaneous-reserve share pricing as a potentially high-impact price manipulation vector. Its interaction with Multipool liquidity and caller-directed withdrawals makes it the highest-priority remaining contract for determining whether an attacker can distort reserves or spot values and extract value from LP share accounting. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every deposit, withdrawal, share-minting, share-burning, reserve snapshot, and deviation-check path; identify all price and reserve inputs and whether they can be manipulated within a transaction or across calls; verify consistency between Dispatcher accounting and actual Multipool/token balances; and conclude whether a concrete price manipulation exploit exists, or document why the pricing and withdrawal controls prevent it.

focus_areas: Whether strategy-selected weights or position ranges can be manipulated to distort pool valuation or share pricing
Whether strategy updates can redirect liquidity toward manipulable pricing sources or trusted fee pools
Whether owner-controlled strategy changes lack price-impact, TWAP, or accounting safeguards
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: MultiStrategy is an unanalyzed stateful component whose owner-controlled strategy and weight selection directly influence Multipool liquidity allocation and therefore price-sensitive reserves and LP-share valuation. It is especially promising given the existing hypotheses around attacker-influenced ranges and instantaneous reserve-based accounting. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every strategy update, weight calculation, multipool interaction, and trusted fee-pool dependency; determine whether any attacker-controllable price or allocation input can cause manipulated valuation or share pricing; conclude with evidence of a concrete price-manipulation path or document why the controls prevent one.

focus_areas: Multipool creation parameters and initial pricing configuration
Validation of underlying pools, tokens, fee tiers, and trusted pool relationships
Whether attacker-controlled deployment inputs can establish manipulable reserves, ranges, or oracle assumptions
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: Factory is an unanalyzed state-creation component that can determine the pools and parameters later used for pricing, while existing hypotheses identify reserve-, range-, and instantaneous-price manipulation risks. Reviewing its deployment-time validation may reveal whether an attacker can create or register a configuration that bypasses those protections. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every external entry point that creates or registers a Multipool, identify all price-relevant inputs and validation checks, and determine whether any caller can establish attacker-controlled pricing sources or parameters. Conclude with either a concrete price-manipulation path and impact or documented evidence that Factory inputs are sufficiently constrained and trusted.

items.goal: Vulnerability analysis of Approved swap target/router
focus_areas: Whether approved swap targets can manipulate token prices or pool reserves used for valuation
Slippage, minimum-output, deadline, and quoted-price enforcement during swaps
Whether arbitrary calldata, callbacks, or routes allow execution at attacker-controlled prices
How swap results affect Multipool reserve accounting, TWAP checks, and share pricing
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: The router is an uncompleted external component at the boundary between operator-controlled rebalancing and reserve-based valuation. Price manipulation through an approved target could distort token balances or execution prices and then affect deposits, withdrawals, or subsequent strategy decisions. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every swap-target call and its inputs/outputs; verify that execution is constrained by an independent oracle or TWAP, strict slippage and deadline checks, and exact token-flow accounting; conclude whether an attacker can profitably alter valuation or LP-share pricing, or document why manipulation is prevented.

items.goal: Vulnerability analysis of ERC20 token reserve integration
focus_areas: How token balances, transfers, rebasing, fee-on-transfer behavior, and direct token donations affect reserve-based share pricing
Whether reserve reads can diverge from economically attributable liquidity before deposits, withdrawals, or rebalances
Whether token accounting permits temporary balance manipulation that changes LP share value or withdrawal amounts
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: Core contracts are already covered, while the ERC20 integration remains a distinct price-sensitive boundary: reserve-based pricing appears to rely on token balances and may be affected by unsolicited transfers or non-standard token behavior. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every balance and transfer used in deposit, withdrawal, valuation, and rebalance pricing; determine whether an attacker can manipulate those values within a transaction or across state transitions; document a concrete exploit path or conclude that all relevant token behaviors are safely constrained.

items.goal: Vulnerability analysis of Uniswap V3 factory
focus_areas: Verify that all pools used for pricing and liquidity operations are canonical factory deployments
Check whether pool identity, token ordering, fee tier, and tick-spacing assumptions can be bypassed or cause pricing to use an unintended pool
Assess whether factory lookups permit attacker-controlled or economically manipulable pool selection
items.reasoning: WHY NOW: The core pool, dispatcher, and strategy components have already been reviewed, but the factory boundary remains a distinct uncompleted external dependency that determines which Uniswap V3 pool is trusted for price-sensitive operations. An incorrect or insufficiently constrained factory lookup could redirect pricing to a thinly liquid or attacker-influenced pool. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every factory lookup and pool-validation path, confirm canonical address and parameter enforcement, and determine whether any attacker can cause price-sensitive logic to use an unintended or manipulable pool; document the result or rule out a price-manipulation impact.
